Reusable Filters work perfectly. - I love the Keurig coffee maker, but had a hard time finding coffee my wife and I both liked for a price we wanted to pay. Great K-Cup Alternative - I started purchasing loose ground coffee and wanted reusable K-cups so I don't have to purchase a separate coffee machine. I'm able to use this with my regular sized Keurig, but need to remove the inner plastic ring for my Keurig Mini Plus in order for this cup to fit. It takes a bit of testing with different types of ground coffee to figure out how much to fill the cup with to have the maximum coffee flavor and strength without getting coffee sludge at the bottom of your cup. I wish this cup would have a marker on the inside to indicate how much to fill it up to. Another con is that the top of the cap doesn't lock or snap shut. If you're like me and wanted to prefill the cups every 4 days so you can grab and go, I recommend putting it in a glass airtight container (if you want to be more eco-friendly) or else the coffee might lose its flavor from the air exposure. Aside from that, I don't have any other complaints about the product. The metal mesh is fine enough to keep most coffee grounds out of your cup. If you want a ground free coffee, you may need to put a paper coffee filter in your cup because the finest grounds will still fall through the mesh.

In comparison to the Keurig universal K-cup, I would say I prefer the universal K-cup more. I like my coffee to be strong and bold with flavor. K-cup Keurig sells has a larger capacity to hold more coffee grounds that allows me to get that result I want with minimal to no sludge (although requires removal of the plastic ring for both of my Keurigs to fit). If you are picky with your coffee, I would recommend the one Keurig sells (even though it's more expensive). If you want a simple and quick cup of coffee, be more eco-friendly, or want to have a multiple amount of K-cups on hand to fill, I think this product will work great for you.

When done, throw into the compost pile - The Melitta Tea Filters, 40-Count (Pack of 6) is a wonderful way to create tea bags, spice bags, bath salt bags, or whatever you can think of for a secure and economical system. I generally place loose tea leaves with herbs and spices inside an unbleached bag, then put it into a teapot. After adding hot water and waiting for the prescribed time period, I easily remove the bag and have a pot of tea with a minimal amount of residue in the brew. Because a filled bag will remain open, I've also created some gifts by attaching a cotton string and little hand decorated tag to the bags. For the unsealed bag, be careful that the longer end does not hang over the edge of a cup, mug or teapot too much or you'll run the risk of the hot water being absorbed all the way to the upper edge, saturating it and possibly dripping onto the table top. This happened to me once because I forgot to retrieve the bag and the teapot sat for about a half hour. The bags can also be used for mulling spices because they are rather large. I love them!

Not Truly Custom Fit & Will Cost You $10+ To Return - Look at the product photos carefully before purchasing. These are NOT CUSTOM FIT in the way you might reasonably assume. You have the option of choosing from dozens of different stove models which gives the impression your set will be cut to fit the specific-sized burners on your specific model stove while protecting other areas of the stove top - not so!

Instead, these "protectors" are apparently made to fit various STYLES of stoves. For example, our style stove has two burners on each side and a griddle in the center, so we were sent two side panels, each with two holes, and a center panel with one hole. That is where the "custom" aspect of this product ends, because the sizes of the holes are waaaay bigger in diameter than the burners, leaving large areas of our stove top (ironically, areas highly likely to receive spills) unprotected. Additionally, some areas of the protectors' borders are so narrow that any spilled food might as easily land on the stove top as on the protectors.

The fact that the seller does not pay for return shipping makes me to believe they do not back up their product (our local post office told us that although the package is super light--which would normally qualify for 1st class shipping--this item's oversized packaging requires it be returned via Priority shipping, costing nearly $11).

Bottom line: this would be a great product if were made by company with the desire to do the job right.

Therefore, I didn't expect much, but wanted something that was easier to keep clean. Depending upon how much heat is required in the house (1800 square ft on one level) the humidity stays above 30% and goes as high as 40%. I keep the unit centrally located and close to a return air grill. Something I think is weird is that one of the tanks drains faster than the other, even if I swap the sides. And I do make sure the water drains the same from both. But this hasn't really been a problem. I just keep the faster draining tank on the side that's easiest to put on and take off. I clean the unit as recommended.. It's a lot easier than my old swamp cooler. Does not filter water in a measurable way. - Aqua-Pure filters are made in the US under license from the patent holder. This is a cheap Chinese knock-off of uncertain quality. Do not buy this POS if you want a real Aqua-Pure filter.

UPDATE: After seller insisted in Questions that this filter is made in the USA and only assembled in China, I decided to test it to see if his additional claim that it works as well as any other filter is true. I tested it with the TDS meter I use to monitor the RO/DI water purifier I use for my saltwater aquarium. First, I ran 5 gallons of water through this filter installed in my Samsung fridge. The water was black for a while, but it cleared up by gallon 3. Instructions say run it for 5 minutes to flush carbon dust, and it took about 7 minutes to pull 5 G.

Measured TDS for the "Aqua-Pure compatible" was 138 PPM. Then I measured unfiltered tap water, and once again got 138 PPM. I repeated the test three times on each water source and got the same figures, +/- 1 PPM.

Consequently, I know that this device does not filter water at all and is certainly not compatible with Aqua Pure. It works no better than having no filter at all in the fridge.

UPDATE 2: The genuine Aqua Pure doesn't reduce TDS either, so it appears that fridge filters are a waste of money even when they're not falsely promoted.

Worked With Slight Modification - I needed this for a Kenmore double oven gas stove. The proper item (with screw tab that mounts the igniter on its edge) was $112 and up. This one worked fine with a minor modification. I had to carefully bend the screw tab downward in order to mount it on its edge. The other tab had to be cut off; which I did with a Dremel tool using a diamond cutoff wheel. Took all of about 5 minutes. I removed the plug from the old igniter and using the included ceramic wire nuts, attached the plug to the new igniter. Another reviewer stated his wire nut did not want to lock on to the wires and apparently fell off, shorting and knocking out his control board. I experienced similar but remedied the problem by nipping (shortening) the bare wires. He apparently had his wire a bit too long and it bottomed out in the wire nut before it could grip and lock on. After nipping off about 1/16th in. the nut tightened properly and securely. The oven now works just fine. Note* As others have stated, just because your igniter glows does not mean it is good....it may not be getting hot enough to activate the temperature sensor to turn on the gas.
